summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend smoke test for Athena Education ERP (multi-tenant SaaS). 35/36 pytest tests pass. Only failure is /api/auth/refresh returning 500 when called twice for the same user within 1 second — a real production bug (JWT refresh tokens generated in the same second have identical payloads → identical sha256 hash → UniqueViolation on refresh_tokens.token_hash). Frontend loads well: landing/login/register/dashboard/super-admin all render, all sidebar navigation testids resolve, dashboard shows 6 KPI cards + 2 charts, multi-tenancy isolation verified, RBAC 403 enforcement verified, faculty auto-creates user+role, billing mock-pay upgrades plan, audit logs populated. AI chat endpoint actually returned 200 (Emergent LLM key has budget after all).

critical.issue: Returns 500 IntegrityError (UniqueViolation on refresh_tokens.token_hash) when two refresh calls happen for the same user within the same second. Root cause: create_refresh_token() in app/core/security.py encodes {sub, tid, exp, iat, type} — no jti claim — so within a 1-second window the JWT string is byte-identical, and sha256(token) collides with an existing row. Fix: add a unique jti (uuid4 hex) claim in _encode(), OR use datetime.now with microsecond precision, OR wrap the insert in try/except IntegrityError and rotate.

issues: Recharts logs 4x console warnings 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' on first render — cosmetic only, charts render correctly after data arrives. Consider giving ResponsiveContainer an explicit min-height.

action_items: FIX: /api/auth/refresh IntegrityError — add `jti` (uuid4) claim to JWT payload in app/core/security.py _encode() so refresh tokens are always unique, even within the same second.
OPTIONAL: Add min-height to Recharts ResponsiveContainer on dashboard to silence -1 width/height warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: app/core/security.py create_refresh_token(): missing unique claim (jti). Two calls within the same second produce identical tokens → same sha256 hash → DB UniqueViolation. Also blocks any legitimate re-issue during the same second.

app/api/v1/billing.py mock_pay(): stores plan as free-form string parsed from invoice description ('Upgrade to pro'). Fragile — better to persist the plan on the Invoice row at creation and read it back.

Backend tests: /api/auth/me correctly returns permissions/roles/organization — no _id/ObjectId issues (Postgres). RBAC dependency require_permissions returns 403 for users with zero roles (verified).

Frontend: all requested data-testids (login-submit-btn, dashboard-page, students-page, faculty-page, attendance-page, marks-page, roles-page, ai-chat-page, analytics-page, billing-page, super-admin-page) are present and resolve.

rca_of_the_issue: TestAuth.test_refresh fails with 500. Backend log shows: sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError: (psycopg2.errors.UniqueViolation) duplicate key value violates unique constraint 'ix_refresh_tokens_token_hash'. The offending flow: _issue_tokens() calls create_refresh_token(user.id, user.organization_id) which encodes JWT payload {sub, tid, exp, iat (second precision), type:'refresh'}. When two refresh requests arrive within the same second, JWT payload is byte-identical → hashed token identical → INSERT into refresh_tokens table hits the unique index and raises IntegrityError → 500. Mitigation: add `jti: uuid.uuid4().hex` in app/core/security.py::_encode(). Reproduction: `curl -X POST $URL/api/auth/refresh -d '{"refresh_token":"<valid>"}'` twice within 1s of each other with the SAME source token — first succeeds, second returns 500.
